node.title: SQL queries
node.why: The analyst must retrieve and combine load, generation, and outage records from database tables.

citation.quote: Write SQL queries against our historian

checkpoints: An INNER JOIN returns rows only when matching keys exist in both tables.
GROUP BY aggregates rows sharing a column value, allowing aggregate functions per group.
A WHERE clause filters rows before grouping, affecting which data is aggregated.
Using indexes on join columns speeds up query execution by reducing row scans.

node.title: Python pandas
node.why: Python with pandas is used to clean, transform, and analyze time-series data for reporting.

citation.quote: working knowledge of Python with pandas

checkpoints: The read_csv function loads tabular data into a DataFrame, parsing delimiters automatically.
The .groupby method groups rows by column values and applies aggregate functions.
.fillna replaces missing values with specified constants or methods like forward fill.
Vectorized operations on DataFrames execute without explicit Python loops, improving performance.

node.title: Statistics fundamentals
node.why: Statistical concepts such as error metrics and seasonality are used to evaluate forecast performance.
checkpoints: Mean absolute error averages absolute differences between predicted and observed values.
Seasonality refers to regular, periodic fluctuations in a time series.
Standard deviation measures spread of data around the mean.

node.title: Power-grid supply-demand
node.why: Understanding how generation and load are balanced informs analysis of grid performance and outages.

citation.quote: supply and demand are balanced on a power grid

checkpoints: Supply must equal demand plus losses at every instant to maintain grid frequency.
Dispatch decisions prioritize low-cost generation sources while respecting transmission constraints.
Imbalance charges are applied when actual generation deviates from scheduled amounts.
Reserve capacity is held to handle unexpected outages or demand spikes.

node.title: Technical writing
node.why: Clear, non-technical explanations are required for metrics, reports, and documentation meant for non-analysts.

citation.quote: Clear writing for people who are not analysts

checkpoints: Plain language replaces jargon with common terms to improve reader comprehension.
Structured documents use headings, lists, and tables to organize information logically.
Consistent tense and active voice make explanations clearer and more direct.
Providing a summary at the beginning gives readers a quick overview of content.

node.title: Database transactions
node.why: Transactions guarantee that invoices and their payments are saved atomically.

citation.quote: Use transactions so that an invoice

checkpoints: A transaction groups multiple statements so either all commit or none do, ensuring atomicity.
If a statement fails, issuing ROLLBACK reverts all changes made in the transaction.
Isolation levels control visibility of intermediate transaction data to other concurrent sessions.

node.title: A/B test design
node.why: Designing A/B tests determines which product changes should be shipped.

citation.quote: Design and analyse A/B tests: choose a primary metric

checkpoints: An A/B test compares two variants by assigning participants randomly to each group.
Randomization reduces selection bias, ensuring observed differences are attributable to the variants.
The primary metric defines the outcome that determines which variant performs better.

node.title: Delivering constructive feedback
node.why: To improve agent behavior through targeted criticism.

citation.quote: Give difficult feedback to team members

checkpoints: Effective feedback separates behavior from the person to focus on observable actions.
Specific examples in feedback reduce ambiguity and increase likelihood of change.
Delivering feedback promptly after the observed behavior prevents memory distortion.
Feedback that includes a clear action item creates a measurable improvement path.
